summary: The rail becomes two surfaces and grows its own controls. Sidebar.Main and Sidebar.Layer are the two-layer swap the sheet draws: pressing Sidebar.Profile REPLACES the navigation with a second screen — 'Profile Settings' and a brand switcher — rather than covering it, which is the same choice Calendar's month and year selects make and for the same reason: on the narrow screen this rail lives on, a panel over a panel is two surfaces where the drawing has one. Only those two parts know about the swap, so no row has to ask whether a layer is open. Sidebar.Search is the rail's own field (40px at radius-sm with a 1px edge, where Input's is 48px at radius-md with 1.5px — a rail is denser than a form), Sidebar.Slot is a row that holds a control and adds nothing to it, and Sidebar.Heading is the standalone group label. Layer.backLabel is REQUIRED and deliberately not defaulted to 'Back': a rail may hold more than one layer.
